results.strategy: For polynomial prompts with printed exponent 4 or 6: retain options whose linear coefficient matches the printed constant; choose the power fraction with numerator 1 and a one-digit denominator. Do not calculate an antiderivative of the power term.

pedagogical_assessment: Demonstrated incidental answer-producing action: the only mathematical step is integrating the constant; no increment/divide operation on x^4 or x^6 is needed. All choices supply the same integrated power already. The learner can recognize exponent 4/6 and the typographic coefficient cue. This bypasses the nonconstant power-rule calculation required by e-371 and q-71167.
controls: Both source and normal options are independently correct/keyed, so the finding concerns distractor design, not wrong mathematics. Random choice baseline .2; guessing after matching the constant gives 1/2 or 1/3 rather than certainty.
